A matched ablation showed that patient-temporal pairing improved external mortality and heart failure AUROC over generic self-supervision by 7.0% and 9.4% on HEEDB-Boston and 8.9% and 9.3% on HEEDB-Atlanta. These findings indicate that pretraining-objective design greatly influences downstream transfer alongside model and data scale, and that in-domain performance alone is i

413c1a371e57b80b36589e6a.title_original: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
413c1a371e57b80b36589e6a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12942v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A churn model is useful through the customers it selects for a retention offer: the better model is the one whose selection makes the campaign more profitable. Tabular foundation models (TFMs), pretrained networks that predict from a table of labelled examples without being trained on it, were recently reported to decisively outperform tree ensembles for churn. That comparison, however, used untuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) and ranking metrics only. We ask whether the advantage holds against tuned GBDTs when models are judged by expected campaign profit and by the reliability of their probabilities. Four TFMs (TabPFN-2.5, TabPFN-3.5, TabPFN-3.5-Fast, TabICL v2) face LightGBM, XGBoost and CatBoost tuned with Optuna on validation AUC, on five public telecom datasets, three from real operators, with 10 repeated splits each and 20 pre-declared comparisons tested with a corrected t-test and Holm correction. TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more expected maximum profit (EMP) than each tuned GBDT on two datasets, Cell2Cell (1.9%) and Iranian (7.6%). On Orange it is ahead in every split (14.3%), but not significantly after correction, and no TFM differs significantly from the GBDTs on the two fictional datasets. Across 27 assumed combinations of customer value, incentive cost and acceptance rate, TabPFN-3.5 stays ahead on all three real-operator datasets, though the size of its gain varies widely. Retuning the GBDTs on EMP moved

d5ca9308efeac3800bab1cd8.title_original: RBLA+: Efficient Rank-Specific LoRA Adapter Extraction for Federated Fine-Tuning with Heterogeneous Clients
d5ca9308efeac3800bab1cd8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12961v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Federated fine-tuning with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) reduces communication and computational overhead by training and exchanging compact trainable LoRA factors. Clients may use different LoRA ranks to meet adapter communication budgets and accommodate different local adaptation needs. The server must process these differences during aggregation and construct adapters at each client's rank for local training. We distinguish pre-aggregation alignment, which handles factor dimensions and scaling conventions before aggregation and rank-specific LoRA adapter extraction, which constructs client-sized pairs from the aggregated global model. Two common approaches to rank-specific extraction are direct rank truncation and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of the dense update. Direct prefix truncation keeps the leading columns of one aggregated factor and the corresponding rows of the other. It is cheap but can increase reconstruction error. The dense SVD approach first forms the product of aggregated LoRA factors. It then decomposes this matrix and retains the leading singular components to construct adapters at the target rank. This gives the optimal rank-constrained approximation in Frobenius norm but incurs significant computational overhead. To address this trade-off, we propose RBLA+ as an extension of RBLA. It uses established compact QR/core-SVD decomposition to minimize Frobenius error for the extracted LoRA update without

e5fe98d6fd1232f9897f5891.title_original: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
e5fe98d6fd1232f9897f5891.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13015v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more ofte

598d84682e25018d2d955b11.title_original: APS-VLA: Action-Guided and Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
598d84682e25018d2d955b11.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13030v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have demonstrated strong generalization in robotic manipulation, yet processing dense visual tokens often incurs high inference latency. Visual token pruning offers a practical way to reduce this cost, but identifying a compact set of tokens that preserves reliable action generation remains challenging. Existing methods largely rely on static or immediate heuristic cues to estimate token importance. We introduce APS-VLA, a framework that learns visual token selection from robot demonstrations while keeping the pretrained VLA backbone frozen. A lightweight Decision Influence Estimator scores tokens conditioned on current visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioception. Its training combines two complementary signals: action supervision matches both the full-input policy predictions and demonstrated actions, while an auxiliary visual transition objective uses demonstrated actions to predict subsequent visual features from the selected representation. At deployment, the estimator performs a single hard selection and packing step before the policy's native action-generation procedure; the auxiliary predictor is removed. Experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO and with $\pi_{0.5}$ and XR-1 on RoboCasa365 demonstrate inference acceleration with modest changes in task success. Across five real-world tasks on two dual-arm platforms, APS-VLA reduces mean policy inference laten

9bc3590a0d1b68535d15c242.title_original: Personalized Memory Rubrics: Learning What to Remember per User via Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment
9bc3590a0d1b68535d15c242.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14017v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Long-horizon personalized agents maintain an evolving memory by continuously deciding what to add, modify, or discard. However, learning an optimal update policy remains challenging. Conventional training relies solely on terminal question-answering accuracy, yielding a coarse feedback signal that treats all intermediate updates identically. Furthermore, update utility is inherently user-specific, as identical memory actions may yield opposite effects across different user personas. Existing methods fail to address this heterogeneity, relying on globally shared evaluation standards with at most a single scalar intermediate reward. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{Personalized Memory Rubrics} (\textbf{PMR}), a framework that translates terminal feedback into fine-grained, per-step, and per-user credit assignment. PMR decomposes evaluation into a universal layer capturing cross-persona failure patterns and a per-user adaptive layer modeling individual traits as a specialized delta over the universal baseline. Through \textbf{Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment}, PMR redistributes credit at the token level, selectively amplifying validated decisions on successful trajectories while falling back to standard policy optimization on failed ones to avoid unreliable attribution. The rubric and memory policy \textbf{co-evolve} in a closed loop with anti-circularity guarantees. Crucially, PMR incurs zero inference overhead,

9bd1b76f01959f1c63eb4bcd.title_original: Ensemble Modeling for Time Series Forecasting: an Adaptive Robust Optimization Approach
9bd1b76f01959f1c63eb4bcd.excerpt: arXiv:2304.04308v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate time-series forecasting is critical for many problems involving temporal data. Ensemble modeling is a well-established technique that leverages multiple predictive models to improve accuracy and robustness, since a single predictor's performance can vary widely due to shifts in the underlying data distribution. This paper proposes a new methodology for building robust ensembles of time series forecasting models. Our approach uses Adaptive Robust Optimization (ARO) to construct a linear regression ensemble whose model weights adapt over time. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through synthetic experiments covering eight disturbance scenarios, from no drift to abrupt regime shifts, and real-world applications, including air pollution management, energy consumption forecasting, and tropical cyclone intensity forecasting. In the real-world applications, our adaptive ensembles outperform the best ensemble member in hindsight by 16-26% in root mean square error (RMSE) and 14-28% in conditional value at risk at the 15% level and improve over the other ensemble methods we compare on most metrics. In the synthetic experiments, they have lower mean RMSE than a rolling-ridge comparator in seven of the eight scenarios, significantly in four, while an abrupt regime shift that first appears after model selection remains a limitation.

725a24dbc6d60aaaec43e3fa.title_original: Integrating Fairness and Model Pruning Through Bi-level Optimization
725a24dbc6d60aaaec43e3fa.excerpt: arXiv:2312.10181v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep neural networks achieve high predictive performance but often require substantial computational and storage resources, which motivates model compression techniques such as neural network pruning. Conventional pruning methods, however, can introduce or amplify algorithmic bias and produce disparate outcomes across demographic groups. We study fair model pruning, which seeks sparse models that satisfy fairness criteria while maintaining predictive performance. We characterize fairness using both group accuracy disparity and differences in compression-induced accuracy degradation across demographic groups. We propose a framework that jointly optimizes pruning masks and model weights under fairness constraints, thereby integrating accuracy and fairness into the compression process. We formulate fair pruning as a constrained bi-level optimization problem and derive an efficient optimization procedure. Experiments across multiple datasets, predictive tasks, model architectures, and sparsity levels show that our framework improves the trade-off among fairness, accuracy, and training efficiency relative to the baseline pruning strategies. Compared with the strongest evaluated baselines, BiFP maintains competitive accuracy and fairness while requiring more than 94% fewer training iterations in the real-world experiments.

6ac26eaaa882436de09f8ef5.title_original: Could Mobile AI be Exploited?: Understanding the Exploitations of Trust and Ethics Gap in On-Device Small Language Models
6ac26eaaa882436de09f8ef5.excerpt: arXiv:2406.05364v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we present a very first study to investigate trust and ethical implications of on-device artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on small language models (SLMs) amenable for personal devices like smartphones. While on-device SLMs promise enhanced privacy, reduced latency, and improved user experience compared to cloud-based services, we posit that they might also introduce significant risks and vulnerabilities compared to their on-server counterparts. As part of our study, we conduct a systematic evaluation of the state-of-the-art on-devices SLMs, compared to their on-server counterparts, using well-established trust and ethics frameworks. Our results illustrate that on-device SLMs are significantly less trustworthy and lacks ethical safeguards, specifically demonstrating more stereotypical, unfair, privacy-breaching and harmful content generation behavior. Further, these risks of on-device SLMs could be exploited through Open Knowledge (OkNow) Attacks, and we demonstrated them using potentially unethical vanilla prompts, to which the on-device SLMs answer with valid responses without any filters and without the need for any jailbreaking or prompt engineering. These responses can be abused for various harmful and unethical scenarios like: societal harm, illegal activities, hate, self-harm, exploitable phishing content, disinformation and many others.

8fdd6daf416b5700fc0113ad.title_original: quanda: An Interpretability Toolkit for Training Data Attribution Evaluation
8fdd6daf416b5700fc0113ad.excerpt: arXiv:2410.07158v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Training data attribution (TDA) methods estimate the influence of individual training samples on a model's predictions, offering a principled lens for interpreting neural networks. Despite rapid methodological progress, TDA evaluation remains scattered across papers and rarely reproducible, making fair comparison between methods challenging. We introduce quanda, a Python toolkit that standardizes TDA evaluation. quanda features a comprehensive collection of evaluation metrics and ready-to-use benchmarks spanning image classification, text classification, and language modeling, alongside a uniform interface for integrating diverse TDA implementations. We showcase quanda through a comparative study of existing TDA methods and find that no approach excels uniformly across metrics, with clear trade-offs between ground-truth faithfulness and downstream task performance. By consolidating the tooling around TDA, quanda equips the community to evaluate attribution methods rigorously and reproducibly. The toolkit is thoroughly tested, documented, and available as an open-source library on PyPI and at https://github.com/dilyabareeva/quanda.

3bfb8de8a47b8798fa1ee519.title_original: Hallucination Mitigation using Agentic AI Natural Language-Based Frameworks
3bfb8de8a47b8798fa1ee519.excerpt: arXiv:2501.13946v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hallucinations remain a significant challenge for Generative AI, undermining trust in AI systems and their reliability. This study investigates how orchestrating multiple specialized AI agents can mitigate hallucinations, with a focus on systems that use Natural Language Processing (NLP) for agent interaction. We design a pipeline that feeds 310 prompts, purposefully crafted to induce hallucinations, into a front-end agent; its outputs are reviewed and refined by second- and third-level agents that detect unverified claims, add explicit disclaimers and clarify speculative content. We introduce four novel Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) - Factual Claim Density, Factual Grounding References, Fictional Disclaimer Frequency and Explicit Contextualization Score - aggregated into a Total Hallucination Score (THS) and assessed by a dedicated fourth-level evaluator agent. Inter-agent context is carried by the Open Floor Protocol (OFP, formerly OVON, Open Voice Network), whose structured JSON messages let each reviewer pass its assessment of hallucination likelihood, and the reasons behind it, to the next stage. Across the 310 prompts, THS improves by a mean of -0.131 per prompt from the front-end agent to the final reviewer (Cohen's d = 2.38), with lower scores on 302 of 310 prompts. The gain is carried mainly by explicit disclaimers and contextualization, making speculative content more transparent and clearly demarcated fr

90295a503c6a245ab3422245.title_original: ResBench: Benchmarking LLM-Generated FPGA Designs with Resource Awareness
90295a503c6a245ab3422245.excerpt: arXiv:2503.08823v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) are widely used in modern hardware design, yet writing Hardware Description Language (HDL) code for FPGA implementation remains a complex and time-consuming task. Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising tool for HDL generation, but existing benchmarks for LLM-based code generation primarily focus on functional correctness while overlooking hardware resource usage. Furthermore, current benchmarks offer limited diversity and do not fully represent the wide range of real-world FPGA applications. To address these shortcomings, we introduce ResBench, the first resource-focused benchmark explicitly designed to distinguish between resource-optimized and inefficient LLM-generated HDL code. ResBench consists of 56 problems across 12 categories, covering applications from finite state machines to financial computing. Our open-source evaluation framework automatically tests LLMs by generating Verilog code, verifying correctness, and measuring resource usage. The experiments, which primarily analyze Lookup Table (LUT) usage, reveal significant differences among LLMs, demonstrating ResBench's capability to identify models that generate more resource-optimized FPGA designs.

6c3c1f453617ad4a070f54c8.title_original: Breaking the Silence: A Dataset and Benchmark for Bangla Text-to-Gloss Translation
6c3c1f453617ad4a070f54c8.excerpt: arXiv:2504.02293v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gloss is a written approximation that bridges Sign Language (SL) and its corresponding spoken language. Despite a deaf and hard-of-hearing population of at least 3 million in Bangladesh, Bangla Sign Language (BdSL) remains largely understudied, with very limited prior work on Bangla text-to-gloss translation and no publicly available parallel dataset at the time of this work. To address this gap, we construct the first publicly available Bangla text-to-gloss dataset, consisting of 1,000 manually annotated and 4,000 synthetically generated Bangla sentence-gloss pairs, along with 159 expert human-annotated pairs used as a test set. Our experimental framework performs a comparative analysis between several fine-tuned open-source models and a leading closed-source LLM to evaluate their performance in low-resource BdSL translation. GPT-5.4 achieves the best automatic metric scores, while open-source models perform competitively despite being much smaller. This work introduces the first publicly available expert-annotated Bangla text-to-gloss dataset, benchmark and trained model for Bangla text-to-gloss translation. It also demonstrates the effectiveness of systematically generated synthetic data for addressing challenges in low-resource sign language translation.

f32ea731b70a424fbf2d3332.title_original: OpenClassGen: A Large-Scale Corpus of Real-World Python Classes for LLM Research
f32ea731b70a424fbf2d3332.excerpt: arXiv:2504.15564v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Existing class-level code generation datasets are either synthetic (ClassEval: 100 classes) or insufficient in scale for modern training needs (RealClassEval: 400 classes), hindering robust evaluation and empirical analysis. We present OpenClassGen, a large-scale corpus of 324,843 Python classes extracted from 2,970 engineered open-source projects. Each entry pairs a human-written class with its corresponding skeleton, which comprises class and method signatures with associated docstrings, and is enriched with 27 static code metrics covering complexity, coupling, cohesion, and inheritance properties. Unlike prior benchmarks that require repository-level context resolution, OpenClassGen provides self-contained class skeletons that serve as complete generation specifications. We demonstrate the corpus's utility by evaluating three LLMs (GPT-o4-mini, Claude-4-Sonnet, Qwen-3-Coder) on a curated, executable subset of 300 classes, enriched with test suites achieving 58% branch coverage. Results show strong semantic similarity (CodeBERTScore-F3: 0.89) but moderate functional correctness (pass rate: 0.33), with substantial variance across models. This variance, along with diverse class characteristics, confirms that OpenClassGen enables meaningful differentiation of LLM capabilities. The dataset supports diverse use cases, including fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, difficulty modelling, and failure mode analysis. T

ad6f5084b57bc9f49ca548a3.title_original: Simple yet Effective Semi-supervised Knowledge Distillation from Vision-Language Models via Dual-Head Optimization
ad6f5084b57bc9f49ca548a3.excerpt: arXiv:2505.07675v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a practical solution for addressing data scarcity challenges by leveraging unlabeled data. Recently, vision-language models (VLMs), pre-trained on massive image-text pairs, have demonstrated remarkable zero-/few-shot performance that often surpasses SSL approaches due to their exceptional generalization capabilities. This gap motivates us to question: how can we effectively harness the powerful generalization capabilities of VLMs into task-specific models? Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a natural framework for transferring VLM capabilities, but we identify that it suffers from gradient conflicts between supervised and distillation losses. To address this challenge, we propose Dual-Head Optimization (DHO), which introduces dual prediction heads for each distinct signal. We observe that DHO mitigates gradient conflicts, enabling improved feature learning compared to single-head KD baselines, with practical benefits of minimal computational overhead and test-time hyperparameter tuning without retraining. Extensive experiments across 15 datasets show that DHO consistently outperforms KD baselines, often outperforming teacher models with smaller student models. DHO also achieves new state-of-the-art performance on both in-distribution ImageNet semi-supervised learning and out-of-distribution generalization across ImageNet variants. Code and model checkpoints are publicly ava

5d5b7968eb0c13999d8569c1.title_original: Benign Overfitting of Two-Layer ReLU Networks in Fixed Dimension through Localized Initialization
5d5b7968eb0c13999d8569c1.excerpt: arXiv:2505.11621v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Benign overfitting occurs when a model fits noisy training data exactly and still generalizes well. We establish this behavior for finite-width two-layer networks with the standard ReLU activation, trained by gradient flow in fixed dimension. Our data-independent initialization combines Gaussian weights with neurons initially active only on shrinking spherical caps. For uniform spherical inputs and any fixed bounded conditional response law, training and excess risks vanish in probability uniformly over all sufficiently late times. The parameters also converge, with probability tending to one, to an interpolating limit whose excess risk vanishes in probability. We use one schedule depending only on sample size and dimension. Our proof connects the network to a kernel flow whose limit combines ridge regression with localized spikes that fit the training residuals. We give explicit sample-size, width and training-time bounds.

7d470f6069fae0302c87bd4f.title_original: Learning-based Autonomous Oversteer Control and Collision Avoidance
7d470f6069fae0302c87bd4f.excerpt: arXiv:2505.15275v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Oversteer, wherein a vehicle's rear tires lose traction and induce unintentional excessive yaw, poses critical safety challenges. Failing to control oversteer often leads to severe traffic accidents. Although recent autonomous driving efforts have attempted to handle oversteer through stabilizing maneuvers, the majority rely on expert-defined trajectories or assume obstacle-free environments, limiting real-world applicability. This paper introduces a novel end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving approach that tackles oversteer control and collision avoidance simultaneously. Existing E2E techniques, including Imitation Learning (IL), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and Hybrid Learning (HL), generally require near-optimal demonstrations or extensive experience. Yet even skilled human drivers struggle to provide perfect demonstrations under oversteer, and high transition variance hinders the accumulation of sufficient data. Hence, we present Q-Compared Soft Actor-Critic (QC-SAC), a new HL algorithm that effectively learns from immature demonstration data and adapts rapidly to new conditions. To evaluate QC-SAC, we introduce a benchmark inspired by real-world driver training: a vehicle encounters sudden oversteer on a slippery surface and must avoid randomly placed obstacles ahead. Experimental results show that QC-SAC attains near-optimal driving policies, significantly surpassing state-of-the-art IL, RL, and HL baselines. Hardw

fd595aa054cb03f505d81a89.title_original: But what is your honest answer? Aiding LLM-judges with honest alternatives using steering vectors
fd595aa054cb03f505d81a89.excerpt: arXiv:2505.17760v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: LLM-as-a-judge is widely used as a scalable substitute for human evaluation, yet judges are least reliable on subtle dishonesty such as sycophancy and manipulation, where a judge scoring a response in isolation lacks a reference point. We introduce Judge Using Safety-Steered Alternatives (JUSSA), a framework that reduces this evaluator uncertainty using the assessed model's own internal representations. An honesty-promoting steering vector, optimized from a single training example, generates a contrastive alternative against which each response is judged. On a new manipulation dataset with human-validated response pairs, JUSSA improves AUROC for both GPT-4.1 (0.893$\rightarrow$0.946) and Claude Haiku (0.859$\rightarrow$0.929) judges. The gains concentrate almost entirely on the pairs a judge would otherwise misrank. They reverse once a judge has saturated a task and for the weakest judge we test, so contrastive evaluation helps most when a judge is capable enough to use the reference but has not yet saturated the task. A layer-wise analysis further locates steering effectiveness in the middle layers, where model representations of honest and dishonest prompt processing diverge. Our work demonstrates that steering vectors can serve as tools for evaluation rather than for improving model outputs at inference, opening a new direction for white-box auditing.

6ad9276fdfd46f04ad994fad.title_original: Data-Driven Exploration for a Class of Continuous-Time Indefinite Linear--Quadratic Reinforcement Learning Problems
6ad9276fdfd46f04ad994fad.excerpt: arXiv:2507.00358v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study reinforcement learning (RL) for a class of continuous-time stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) control problems, where volatilities depend on both states and controls while states are scalar-valued and there are no running control rewards, the last feature also leading to the so-called indefinite LQ controls. We propose a model-free, data-driven exploration mechanism that adaptively adjusts entropy regularization by the critic and policy variance by the actor. Unlike the constant or deterministic exploration schedules employed in the existing literature, which require extensive tuning for implementations and ignore learning progress during iterations, our adaptive exploratory approach boosts learning efficiency with minimal tuning. Despite its flexibility, our method achieves a sublinear regret bound that matches the best-known model-free results for this class of LQ problems, which were previously derived only with fixed exploration schedules. Numerical experiments demonstrate that adaptive explorations accelerate convergence and improve regret performance compared to the non-adaptive model-free and model-based counterparts.

c69b7e321f22ccc9057a4ded.title_original: Symbolic Branch Networks: Tree-Inherited Neural Models for Interpretable Multiclass Classification
c69b7e321f22ccc9057a4ded.excerpt: arXiv:2507.01781v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Symbolic Branch Networks (SBNs) are neural models whose architecture is derived directly from an ensemble of decision trees. Each root-to-parent-of-leaf decision path is mapped to a hidden neuron, while the matrices W1 (feature-to-branch) and W2 (branch-to-class) encode the structural relationships induced by the teacher ensemble. This provides an explicit correspondence between teacher branches and neural components, enabling feature-level and branch-level interpretation while retaining the flexibility of gradient-based optimization. The primary configuration studied in this work trains the teacher-derived feature-to-branch matrix W1 through gradient-based learning while keeping the branch-to-class matrix W2 fixed; this configuration is denoted SBN1,0. Across 29 multiclass tabular datasets, this configuration improves upon the teacher ensemble on 28 of 29 datasets, increasing mean accuracy from 84.0% to 87.9%. For reference, XGBoost and TabPFN achieve mean accuracies of 87.3% and 91.3%, respectively, on the same datasets. A one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on dataset-level mean accuracies indicates a statistically significant improvement of SBN1,0 over the teacher ensemble (p=4.71x10-7). Beyond predictive performance, SBN provides an explicit structural basis for interpretation.
