ca9a7d74ee9cef154d6d9f48.title_original: D'BEAST: Logged Bad Experiences as Explanation for Autonomous Driving Agents
ca9a7d74ee9cef154d6d9f48.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning agents learn from mistakes, yet their decisions can be difficult to trace back to those experiences. We investigate whether a tabular agent's decisions can be explained by its bad experiences, defined as the training transitions associated with safety or task events. A fixed training log is replayed from the same initial Q-table under three conditions. FULL retains all updates, SKIP omits bad-experience updates, and NEUTRALIZE retains those updates without their event penalties. We illustrate the method on six classic Markov decision processes and evaluate it in closed-loop driving in CARLA. On the full driving task, FULL reached the goal from 33 of 40 test starts, whereas SKIP and NEUTRALIZE reached it from none, indicating that the bad experiences carry decision-relevant information. At the local level, for 47 decisions shortly before a failure of SKIP or NEUTRALIZE, removing or neutralizing a small group of bad experiences, with a median size of one, caused the trained agent to select the failing policy's action in 46 cases. For this agent, the results indicate that its decisions can be explained by its bad experiences.

fcfc95def7dc183fd75f4f86.title_original: Improving fine-grained expressivity of graph neural networks
fcfc95def7dc183fd75f4f86.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20020v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This thesis investigates the expressive power of neural networks for structured data, focusing on graph neural networks and symmetry-aware architectures. We present four main contributions. First, we characterize the generic expressive power of geometric message-passing neural networks on sparse graphs and introduce EGenNet, an architecture achieving the corresponding guarantees. Second, we use representation theory to characterize linear layers equivariant to multiple permutations, including wreath-product symmetries. Third, we study permutation-invariant set representations that preserve containment, establish dimensional bounds and impossibility results, and introduce MASNet. Finally, we propose FSW-GNN, a message-passing architecture combining strong expressivity and bi-Lipschitz stability guarantees with strong empirical performance on long-range graph-learning tasks. Together, these results provide a broader understanding of how neural architectures can preserve the geometric, algebraic, order-theoretic, and metric structure of their inputs.

d547f72a3a5de6866fe618b2.title_original: acuSimNet: Multi-View Self-Occlusion-Awared Visibility Learning for Cranio-Cervical Acupuncture Points
d547f72a3a5de6866fe618b2.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The localization of acupuncture points (acupoints) in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) presents unique challenges since they are defined by abstract principles rather than distinct anatomical landmarks. Existing approaches are typically constrained to single view or rely on indirect calculations of relative positions with respect to other landmarks, thereby overlooking human anatomical variations. Furthermore, acupoint visibility assessment, which determins whether points are occluded by human itself, hair, clothing, or other objects, has received limited attention in practical applications. Acupoint localization itself does not require 3D reconstruction, but inferring their occlusion relationships with anatomical surfaces does, which adds computational cost and limits real-time inference. In this work, we introduce acuSimNet, an efficient hierarchical multi-task learning architecture for multi-view, self-occlusion-aware visibility prediction of acupoints, achieving 99.97% accuracy on the validation set. Our approach also addresses the challenges of high-dimensional classification (174 acupoints in cervicocranial region), negative convergence issues for visible acupoints, and inter-task scheduling optimization, resulting in substantially accelerated convergence. We improved the training efficiency from the exisiting methods of 3000 epochs to achieve 99% validation accuracy, to our optimized framework achieving 90% accuracy i

895ff722eb054248b64486d1.title_original: Security of Deep Research Agents: Attack Surface, Defenses, Benchmarks, and Agenda Seeding against Research Planning
895ff722eb054248b64486d1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep research and agentic search agents autonomously retrieve content from the open web and generate reports with citations, and their outputs are often taken directly as research conclusions. This paper systematizes security research in this area along four stages, namely retrieval, planning, evidence integration, and report generation. We present a unified threat model, a taxonomy of attacks and defenses, and a review of evaluation benchmarks, and we align the area dimension by dimension with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) poisoning, prompt injection, and generative engine optimization (GEO). Coding 34 primary studies shows that only 26.5% of them involve the planning stage, and none performs an end-to-end poisoning evaluation on commercial products. To address this gap, we propose the agenda seeding attack, in which the attacker writes no instructions and only introduces a fictitious evaluation metric. Across 3,520 sandboxed research runs under the same budget, GEO and prompt injection are nearly ineffective, whereas agenda seeding makes the attacker's target the top pick in 16% to 28% of reports. Injection detection and query anchoring fail against it, verification prompting hurts utility, and our proposed provenance tagging preserves utility but can be bypassed by multi-site bait. Finally, we propose eight research directions.
895ff722eb054248b64486d1.title_ko: 심층 리서치 에이전트의 계획을 겨냥한 ‘의제 심기’ 공격 연구
895ff722eb054248b64486d1.summary_ko: 연구진은 심층 리서치 에이전트의 보안을 네 단계로 체계화하고, 가짜 평가 지표로 연구 계획을 유도하는 ‘의제 심기’ 공격을 제안했다. 격리 환경에서 3,520회 실행한 결과, 공격자가 원하는 대상이 보고서의 최우선 추천으로 선택된 비율은 16~28%였다고 보고했다. 제안한 출처 태깅 방어도 여러 사이트를 이용한 유인으로 우회될 수 있었다.
895ff722eb054248b64486d1.background_ko: 기존 연구 34편 중 계획 단계를 다룬 비율이 26.5%에 그치고 상용 제품의 종단 간 오염 평가가 없다는 공백을 다루기 위한 연구다.

7214ea17affbf15b56ffe860.title_original: Clinician Assessment of Laryngeal Disease with Auditory AI before Laryngoscopy: A Paired Reader Study
7214ea17affbf15b56ffe860.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Background: Before laryngoscopy, clinicians assess the likely cause of hoarseness and whether to suspect a precancerous or malignant lesion. We evaluated both in a held-out test set and a later cohort. Accuracy rose 14.7 points when the model was correct and fell 8.7 when incorrect. Provisional-category accuracy was 72% in held-out testing and 67% in temporal validation. The malignancy alert flagged 85.7% and 86.8% of precancerous or malignant lesions. Sensitivity for precancerous or malignant lesions increased from 53.9% to 75.0% after AI-assisted review (d

537cc63fedf305904bf02a13.title_original: The Silent Cost of Conversation History in LLM Reasoning
537cc63fedf305904bf02a13.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in multi-turn information systems accumulate their own earlier replies and a growing task state. We asked whether this conversation history lowers accuracy, and whether process-level quality metrics warn before it does. Each analysis was fixed before its outcomes were computed. In Study 1, on 48 sharded math tasks, retaining its replies lowered final success by 0.21 for GPT-4o-mini and 0.29 for Mistral-7B (Holm-adjusted p = 0.026 and 0.004); Llama-4 Scout showed the same direction, not significant. Study 2 introduces CDR-Stream, 100-turn state-tracking dialogues with an exact answer per turn and per-model difficulty calibration. With the full history, accuracy fell from about 0.6 to 0.1 within twenty turns at matched difficulty, whereas a solver-verified state summary kept it 0.52-0.59 higher (Holm-adjusted p less than 0.001). Consistency and logical coherence fell far less than accuracy, and stability rose. None of these metrics, a paired readiness measure or calibrated single-stream drift detectors gave robust, model-general early warning, although in Study 2 the repeat-based metrics were complete only for GPT-4o-mini. In the monitors we tested, a single 100-turn stream had power only for very large drops. Systems built on LLMs should keep task state outside the transcript and monitor across sessions.

641a81af5380c4cf3178b65a.title_original: FRAAC: A French Multimodal Large Language Model and Dataset forPictogram-Based Augmentative and Alternative Communication
641a81af5380c4cf3178b65a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pictograms are a core modality in augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), yet recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) cannot reliably interpret or produce pictogram sequences. Two obstacles explain this gap: the absence of a standardized pictogram grammar and the scarcity of parallel text-pictogram data. We introduce Retrieval-Augmented Pictogram Selection (RAPS), an annotation method that refines a rule-based transcription system's output with LLM-based concept extraction and retrieval over a pictogram vocabulary, handling cases where hand-written rules fail (named entities, numbers, polysemous words) without requiring new rules. Applied to French, RAPS yields a synthetic corpus of 1.4 million parallel pairs, of which 300k are publicly released. In a human ranking study where annotators order four pictogram transcriptions of the same sentence, RAPS outperforms the rule-based state of the art. Moreover, we show that standard reference-based metrics separate systems of clearly different quality but fail to rank strong systems against each other. Finally, we build an instruction-tuned model that supports interaction in several AAC modalities: it accepts pictogram or text input and answers in pictograms, speech, or text.

55a5b3742d5467af80bee97b.title_original: Making Preemption Productive in Long-Output LLM Serving
55a5b3742d5467af80bee97b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reasoning LLMs generate long outputs whose key--value (KV) caches occupy GPU memory for minutes. When memory fills, the server preempts requests, and a preempted request can repeatedly lose and recover its state while producing little new output. We call this behavior KV thrashing. In certain cases, existing systems leave more than a fifth of requests stalled for over a minute. Because preemption cannot be avoided without delaying admission, we ask how to make it productive. We present Stint, a serving system that preserves a preempted request's work, bounds how long it waits, and gives it fresh output after it returns. Stint stores fixed-length KV snapshots in a contiguity-first CPU pool with an exact-extent allocator, and moves them with fused K/V gather/scatter kernels and double buffering. Age-based readmission brings stalled requests back, and protection gives them a turn of fresh decoding before another preemption. Remaining-length estimates from decoding hidden states guide victim selection. On olympiad-math replays with Qwen3-32B on H200 GPUs, no request pauses for more than 50 seconds under Stint and p99 time per output token falls by 50.7\% relative to recomputation in the same engine. The replay as a whole finishes 10.7\% sooner (12.0\% higher throughput), because the requests that baselines starve no longer finish last.

07ddaec34d652651ed7e33b4.title_original: SAFER: Navigating the Exploration-Exploitation Dilemma in World-Model-Based Planning for Autonomous Driving
07ddaec34d652651ed7e33b4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An autonomous vehicle must foresee the consequences of its actions, especially in the rare, time-critical situations where crashes happen. A world model offers this foresight, but only within the coverage of its training data, which poses an exploration-exploitation dilemma. Within this coverage a planner can hardly improve on the data, and beyond it the model's errors mislead it. Logs of competent driving rarely contain the failures that would widen the coverage, and agents that learn from interaction gain them only by failing themselves, without being shown what to do instead. We propose SAFER, a framework that learns offline from failures that others make, judged by an expert, and keeps learning online from its own driving. Offline, partially trained agents and scripted, recoverable perturbations Stage failures in simulation, and an expert Annotates every visited state with its action and value, so that much of what the planner explores is covered before it drives. In planning, a chunked latent world model Foresees the consequences fast enough for real-time use, and a risk-aware sampling-based planner Evaluates candidate maneuvers by their return minus a bounded collision penalty. Online, a loop continuously Refines the model wherever this driving leaves the coverage of the offline data. In closed-loop evaluation against the compared methods, SAFER reaches the highest route completion and reward per step on the CARLA Leader

e548dde0278c9c8e69d2f2d5.title_original: MT-RGCN-DTI: A Multi-Task Relational Graph Convolutional Network for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction
e548dde0278c9c8e69d2f2d5.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) has become a very crucial part of drug discovery. With the increase in the data volume, it has become very important to improve prediction accuracy by integrating multiple data sources. In this regard, utilising multiple resources in the form of heterogeneous information network to address DTI prediction can be rewarding. In this work, we propose a heterogeneous information network based multi-task DTI prediction model which leverages the advantages of relation graph convolutional network (RGCN). To achieve this, the model employs drug-target interaction network, drug-drug similarity network and protein-protein similarity network to construct a heterogeneous information network. Moreover, we use a knowledge graph embedding scoring functions to model interactions between drug and targets, specifically DistMult and ComplEx as decoders over the learned node representations. We performed extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets and compared with state-of-the-art methods. We observed that the proposed model shows competitive performance, thereby confirming the effectiveness of our approach. The codes and datasets are available at https://github.com/Dheeran-S/MT-RGCN-DTI/.

da4cce5e21095e52724b98d7.title_original: Locational Marginal Pricing of Compute: Co-optimizing Compute and Energy for Transparent Data Center Flexibility
da4cce5e21095e52724b98d7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20116v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Demand from data centers and AI compute is growing rapidly and is increasing stress on the power grid. This load could be flexible through user adjustments and provide relief during energy scarcity events, yet today its flexibility is provided through utility call-ups or system-operator load shedding, and is invisible to the users whose workloads are being curtailed. In this work, we propose to quantify and couple the prices of compute and energy in a single optimization problem. The resulting compute price reflects the marginal cost of the binding constraints and decomposes into components indicating which grid, power, hardware, or service requirement causes a price surge. The economic interpretation updates the price with real-time conditions and gives users a signal for potential flexibility provision. The co-optimization ultimately connects compute and energy markets while providing a signal for relief of stress on both the grid and the compute resources.

78ac323a3ce89a78fb7f519c.title_original: CECAR: Cache & Expert Co-Aware Routing Accelerates On-Device Inference of MoE LLMs
78ac323a3ce89a78fb7f519c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20119v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Despite growing interest in on-device LLM deployment, large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models remain impractical on resource-constrained devices, as sparse expert activation still requires all expert weights to be memory-resident. To address this, we identify three key observations for on-device MoE inference: (a) cache hit rates are fundamentally bounded even under Belady's optimal policy; (b) these bounds are insufficient for low-latency on-device inference; and (c) prior cache-aware routing based on binary cache presence can induce routing instability. Based on these insights, we propose CECAR (Cache & Expert Co-Aware Routing), a MoE inference system that jointly considers expert routing and cache management. Unlike prior cache-aware routing methods, CECAR uses an ML-based cache policy to predict the expected reuse distance of each expert and prioritizes routing and execution toward experts with smaller predicted reuse distances. On the Qwen3-30B-A3B model, CECAR achieves 12.5 tokens/s on a consumer-grade GPU with only 16 GB of VRAM, where non-resident experts are fetched from SSD, delivering a 4.5x speedup over conventional MoE inference and exceeding the decode speed of baselines that keep the entire model fully resident in DRAM. Code is available at https://github.com/hoonki2002/CECAR.
78ac323a3ce89a78fb7f519c.title_ko: CECAR, 캐시와 전문가 선택을 함께 최적화해 기기 내 MoE 추론 가속
78ac323a3ce89a78fb7f519c.summary_ko: CECAR는 전문가별 예상 재사용 거리를 예측해 캐시 관리와 전문가 선택을 함께 최적화하는 MoE 추론 시스템이다. 연구진은 Qwen3-30B-A3B의 비상주 전문가 가중치를 SSD에서 불러오는 방식으로 VRAM 16GB GPU에서 초당 12.5토큰을 달성했으며, 기존 MoE 추론보다 4.5배 빨랐다고 보고했다.
78ac323a3ce89a78fb7f519c.background_ko: MoE는 일부 전문가만 활성화해도 전체 전문가 가중치의 메모리 상주가 요구되며, 기존 캐시 방식만으로는 기기 내 저지연 추론에 한계가 있어 제안됐다.

af404499be6806af39645a15.title_original: Can decision models extract clinical data from cancer pathology reports? An evaluation of accuracy, calibration, and failure modes
af404499be6806af39645a15.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20129v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Decision models are a new class of language model that, instead of generating text, choose one option per question from a fixed list and return a probability for every option. They have not yet been evaluated on clinical text. We evaluated two open-weights decision models, Nimble 9B and Tev1 4B, for extracting 25 fields from 1,113 oral cavity cancer pathology reports from a single centre, against a prospectively maintained clinical database. We compared them with two generative models: Qwen3.5 9B, run locally, and GLM-5.3-flash, run through a cloud API. Tev1 reached a mean field accuracy of 0.917 (95% CI 0.913 to 0.920), the same as Qwen3.5 9B (0.918; p = 0.26), and was four times faster (15 s against 61 s per report). Nimble reached 0.862 and GLM-5.3-flash 0.986. Both decision models matched GLM-5.3-flash on simple dichotomous categories. They were weak on measurements binned into categories, on fields whose correct answer was not reported, and on some complex decisions (e.g. involved margins). We found that the main cause of the inferior performance of Nimble's came from asking 25 questions in one request: with two questions per request, its accuracy improved. Pooled over fields, the returned probabilities were well calibrated (expected calibration error 0.022 and 0.026), but they did not flag systematic errors within single fields. A simulated strategy of sending answers with a probability below 0.94 to GLM-5.3-flash raised

b9bd3e5afc99e0fee2b61ded.title_original: CapCover Filter: Semantic Approximate Membership Queries over Embeddings
b9bd3e5afc99e0fee2b61ded.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20132v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Determining whether an embedding is sufficiently similar to any vector in a vector store without performing a nearest-neighbor search can substantially improve query throughput in vector-store systems. We study Semantic Approximate Membership Queries (SAMQs), which allow queries to be rejected when no indexed vector meets the requested similarity threshold, while guaranteeing no false negatives. We introduce CapCover Filter, a geometric data structure that summarizes a set of embeddings using spherical caps. Its representation is independent of the query threshold, allowing a single filter to support arbitrary thresholds without reconstruction. We evaluate alternative construction and quantization methods, compare CapCover Filter with competing filters, and measure its impact on query throughput. Across five real-world datasets, at a cosine similarity threshold of 0.95, CapCover Filter eliminates approximately 20--100\% of index accesses while using only 2\% of the raw (FP32) embedding memory. When placed before a FAISS flat index, it improves query throughput by up to 382\% and by approximately 116\% on average across the five datasets, while returning the same range-search result. We also evaluate lower similarity thresholds. Our results show that CapCover Filter can substantially improve vector-store throughput when similarity thresholds are tight, retrieval is expensive, and indexed embeddings are highly clustered. 74565352dd1ed4d42433cee5.title_original: Can AI Judge You? An Empirical Audit of Deployment Readiness in LLM-assisted Hiring Systems
74565352dd1ed4d42433cee5.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Delegating resume screening to large language models (LLMs) requires organizations to establish whether they can distinguish candidates by relevant qualifications while allowing only authorized users to change screening rules or approve exceptions. To this end, we develop a system architecture that separates candidate evidence, evaluation, permission controls, and assessment record, and empirically examine two complementary dimensions of its deployment readiness. First, we assess its operational readiness on four LLMs using a controlled experiment on 210 resumes across 14 job roles and six decision interfaces. Second, we assess its compliance readiness by testing how it handles unauthorized user requests and instructions embedded in resumes. We find that operational performance depends on the choice of evaluation interface: scalar scores generally distinguish qualification changes better than simple pass/fail judgments, while comparative judgments are sensitive to presentation order. Explicit permission rules and separation of resume content from instructions reduce unauthorized compliance, to a varying degree of effectiveness across LLMs and usage contexts. Finally, we find that LLM evaluators often diverge between their decisions and offered justifications. Going beyond simply evaluating LLMs for hiring tasks, our framework supports an audit of a fully configured resume evaluation system to enable its deployment decision.

e1624097761b1c544f7b8362.title_original: RoboKit: Accelerating Parallel Differentiable Optimization for Robot Learning
e1624097761b1c544f7b8362.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20185v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present RoboKit, a high-performance, general-purpose toolkit for parallel differentiable optimization in robotics, built on three principles: (i) Performance and flexibility: GPU-parallel multi-seed solvers pair sampling with versatile optimizers, running 2-60$\times$ faster than task-specific baselines across seven tasks; (ii) Geometry, rendering and physics: hybrid and coarse-to-fine representations accelerate collision, differentiable rendering and simulation, optimizing 4096 grasps in 2.97 s; (iii) Integration with learning: costs are differentiable and simulation is parallel, so RoboKit both distills optimization into policies and trains RL; distilled policies run 9-240$\times$ faster at comparable accuracy, and RL reaches a GPU baseline's scores up to 2.1$\times$ sooner on the same simulator.

22232c443594346c23fc2ae9.title_original: Cyber-Secure Wearable, Ultra-Low-Power Networked Sensors for Soldier Health Monitoring: Insights from the CAPSARII project
22232c443594346c23fc2ae9.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The CAPSARII project advances a cyber-secure, ultra-low-power wearable platform and Internet of Battlefield Things (IoBT) framework to support real-time monitoring of military personnel and data-driven decision support. The architecture integrates smart-textile sensing, a body/squad area mesh, edge-deployed AI on secure RISC-V microcontrollers, and cloud/federated analytics for cross-mission learning and comparative studies. Two representative use cases--pilot fatigue and warfighters operating in harsh environments--guide requirements, validation, and interface design (including HUD and haptic feedback). As an initial step toward embedded models, we benchmark stress classification on a public wearable dataset: tree-ensemble baselines achieve state-of-the-art performance for accuracy and F1 (e.g., XGBoost: $\mathrm{Accuracy}=0.901\!\pm\!0.023$, $\mathrm{F1}=0.920\!\pm\!0.019$), while a feature-based Transformer attains the highest AUC ($0.963\!\pm\!0.025$), informing feature-engineering and compression choices for edge deployment. Building on these results, CAPSARII employs HW/SW co-design, model compression (pruning, quantization, distillation), and precision tuning to meet stringent energy and memory budgets; it further investigates Processing-in-Memory accelerators for future efficiency gains. A structured gap analysis highlights the remaining challenges: establishing validation standards for physiological signal quality and

7bccea4077048af5cc363663.title_original: How Specification Explicitness Shapes Failure in LLM-Generated Code
7bccea4077048af5cc363663.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When LLMs turn requirements into code, every underspecified constraint becomes behavior that the model must decide during generation. We test when specifications move beyond structure and begin to control generated behavior. In a controlled experiment, 72 participants implemented and revised Python tasks with an LLM under three levels of specification explicitness. The results show a clear break between lightweight structure and explicit behavioral obligations. Lightweight structure reduced hidden-test failures by only 8.7%. Requiring participants to specify constraints, invariants, negative requirements, edge cases, tie-breaking rules, and exception handling cut failures by 47.2% and reduced the number of distinct failure modes by 20.5%. The largest drops were in failure modes tied to implicit obligations. Invariant violations fell by 66.1%, and unsupported assumptions fell by 59.5%. After a requirement change, specifications with explicit behavioral obligations produced regressions in more submissions, but each affected submission lost less previously correct behavior. Explicit specifications also changed how developers judged generated code. Without explicit obligations, participants overestimated generated-code correctness by about 23 percentage points. With explicit obligations, they produced better code but judged it more cautiously. Thus, the lesson is sharper than "better specifications help." Lightweight structure bar
7bccea4077048af5cc363663.title_ko: LLM 코드 생성, 명시적 동작 요구사항이 실패를 줄인다는 연구
7bccea4077048af5cc363663.summary_ko: 연구진은 참가자 72명이 LLM으로 Python 과제를 구현·수정하는 실험에서 요구사항의 명시 수준에 따른 차이를 비교했다. 단순한 구조화는 숨겨진 테스트 실패를 8.7% 줄이는 데 그쳤지만, 불변 조건·예외 처리 등 동작 의무를 명시하면 실패가 47.2%, 실패 유형 수가 20.5% 줄었다고 보고했다.
7bccea4077048af5cc363663.background_ko: 요구사항에 명시되지 않은 제약은 코드 생성 중 모델이 자체적으로 결정해야 하므로, 명세의 구체성이 생성 코드의 동작을 얼마나 통제하는지 검증했다.
