30105c2655f03adbfe7be9c9.title_original: Suppression Is Not Erasure: Mechanistic Analysis and Reactivation Boundaries of Subspace Projection for LoRA Backdoor Defense
30105c2655f03adbfe7be9c9.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12807v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is widely used to customize large language models, but third-party adapters create supply-chain backdoor risks with under 1% modified parameters. Recent analytical null-space and subspace projection defenses report near-zero static Attack Success Rates (ASR), equating static silence with erasure. We audit subspace-projection defenses across four scales (Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B), three architectures (Qwen2.5, InternLM2.5-1.8B, Spark-X2.6-4B), and five trigger families (suffix, natural phrase, prefix/in-sentence, double-negation syntax, and composite triggers). Statically, module-wise rank-1 trigger-difference projection cuts ASR from 60.4% to 0.0% on standard suites and 70.3% to 0.0% on 1,000 uncontaminated prompts (p = 3.055e-299) in under 5 s. By Theorem 1 (11,880/11,880 module-sample pairs), low-rank bottleneck amplification aligns benign polite-suffix probes with u_1(B) (median cosine 0.8934-0.9705), reaching 0.0% ASR without trigger knowledge. However, static suppression is not erasure. Under 5-sample reactivation, single-round weight-editing baselines rebound to 91.7%-100.0% ASR in Epoch 1 (Fine-Pruning, ANP, NEEDLE, LoRA-Patch; 48.7% for single-round dual projection) and 100.0% by Epoch 2. Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 prove single-sided projection leaves non-zero gradients along u_1 across 168/168 modules (27.2x-31.1x above random expectation), while Haar orthogonal rotation shows Epoch-2 immuni

2f65ce45b48d35d870eae8b1.title_original: EDGChain-E: A Decentralized Git-Based Framework for Versioning Encrypted Energy Data
2f65ce45b48d35d870eae8b1.excerpt: arXiv:2507.01615v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper proposes a new decentralized framework, named EDGChain-E (Encrypted-Data-Git Chain for Energy), designed to manage version-controlled, encrypted energy data using blockchain and the InterPlanetary File System. The framework incorporates a Decentralized Autonomous Organization (DAO) to orchestrate collaborative data governance across the lifecycle of energy research and operations, such as smart grid monitoring, demand forecasting, and peer-to-peer energy trading. In EDGChain-E, initial commits capture the full encrypted datasets-such as smart meter readings or grid telemetry-while subsequent updates are tracked as encrypted Git patches, ensuring integrity, traceability, and privacy. This versioning mechanism supports secure collaboration across multiple stakeholders (e.g., utilities, researchers, regulators) without compromising sensitive or regulated information. We highlight the framework's capability to maintain FAIR-compliant (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) provenance of encrypted data. By embedding hash-based content identifiers in Merkle trees, the system enables transparent, auditable, and immutable tracking of data changes, thereby supporting reproducibility and trust in decentralized energy applications.

8be5824412ae0e206d972e68.title_original: NL-SME: Enhancing Multi-Step Gradient Inversion through Adaptive Two-State Matching
8be5824412ae0e206d972e68.excerpt: arXiv:2509.22082v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training among multiple clients without directly sharing their raw data.However, gradient inversion attacks can exploit the model updates exchanged during training to reconstruct clients' private data.With multiple local training steps, an observed update combines gradients evaluated at changing model states and potentially different mini-batches, while intermediate states remain hidden. Restricting gradient evaluation to a single state on the segment between the initial and final models can exclude states that better fit the accumulated update.We consider reconstruction from an individual client's endpoint models, assuming that the training labels are known.We propose NL-SME, a regularized two-state gradient surrogate for matching multi-step client updates without replaying local training.The surrogate adapts its evaluation center, regularizes its displacement, and averages raw parameter gradients at two shared symmetric states.We evaluate NL-SME against existing gradient inversion methods on FEMNIST and CIFAR-100 with varying numbers of local training steps.The results show improved reconstruction quality, highlighting the privacy risks of sharing individual client updates after multiple local steps.

96e87771de41514c418fb075.title_original: On the Price of Privacy for Language Identification and Generation
96e87771de41514c418fb075.excerpt: arXiv:2604.07238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models train on sensitive user data, so we ask what differential privacy (DP) costs in language learning. We study private language identification and generation in the agnostic statistical setting. For identification, privacy is free: at every fixed $\varepsilon$, pure DP and $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP with $\delta\ge n^{-O(1)}$ keep the non-private rate $\exp(-r(n))$ for every $r(n)=o(n)$. For generation, the price depends on what is public. With a public witness bound, pure DP loses at most a factor $\Theta(\min\{1,\varepsilon\})$ in the exponent, and on suitable two-language collections the optimal rate is $\exp(-\Theta(\min\{1,\varepsilon\}\,n))$. Without such a bound, pure DP can lose the exponential rate itself, already for two languages: every rate $\exp(-o(n))$ stays achievable, but no exponential rate is. On these collections, $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP keeps an exponential rate if and only if $\log(1/\delta)=o(n)$. Three facts about pure DP drive the proofs. It turns a robustness margin into an exponentially small error. It obeys a private form of Le Cam's two-point bound. And it cannot see the absence of a string.

d6967a318368eb6520cf8dba.title_original: Not What a Child Expressed: Auditing the Sign-to-Text Safety Interface in Child-Facing AI
d6967a318368eb6520cf8dba.excerpt: arXiv:2610.07519v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automatic sign language translation (SLT) has entered consumer products, turning American Sign Language into English text for dictation, messaging, and queries put to a conversational assistant. Child-facing AI and platform trust-and-safety tooling decide on text, using filters on minor accounts and grooming classifiers that score chat messages. A signing child who uses SLT therefore reaches these safeguards through a translation. We found no publicly documented system in which the two have been jointly evaluated, and the leading deployed SLT model was neither trained nor formally evaluated on signers under 18. Errors that alter negation, participant roles, secrecy, urgency or help-seeking could change a safety decision without disturbing fluency. This paper proposes a Deaf-informed pre-deployment audit of that boundary, with a failure taxonomy, a sanitised scenario schema, four comparison conditions, and four outcome measures. Auslan is the planned first case study.

def05c6921270af4a276cfd7.title_original: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators
def05c6921270af4a276cfd7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.02376v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present AltoPIR, the first PIR system that exploits the capability of emerging on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX. Unlike existing solutions, AltoPIR achieves high-performance PIR through efficient batching without requiring discrete accelerators. However, the on-CPU accelerator has only a few small registers and shares its core with request handling. As a result, it runs far below its peak rate while its operands arrive from memory, and it remains idle while its core handles requests. To keep the accelerator busy, we design mechanisms that reduce both the memory traffic of a batch and the core cycles spent on each request. Our experimental results show that AltoPIR outperforms existing CPU-based solutions by up to 50.1x.

89051e31262106d745ef3ba4.title_original: Inside Modern Phishing Kits Built to Steal Microsoft 365 Sessions

89051e31262106d745ef3ba4.background_ko: Microsoft 365 로그인 토큰을 탈취해 재사용하면 다중요소 인증을 마친 세션과 클라우드 자원에 접근할 수 있다는 점이 공격에 악용된다.

curation.reason_ko: 다중요소 인증 이후의 Microsoft 365 세션을 노리는 피싱 키트 분석으로 토큰 기반 침해 대응에 유용하다.

13e711f6631054c9334ad4b5.title_original: Microsoft testing Remote Lock for lost or stolen Windows devices

13e711f6631054c9334ad4b5.summary_ko: Microsoft가 Windows 11 Insider Preview에서 기업 관리자가 Intune으로 기기를 원격 잠그는 Remote Lock을 시험하고 있다. 데이터를 삭제하지 않고 모든 활성 세션과 로그인 수단을 차단하며, 재시작하거나 오프라인 상태여도 잠금이 유지된다. 다만 네트워크 격리나 외부 매체 부팅 차단 기능은 아니다.
13e711f6631054c9334ad4b5.background_ko: 기업 IT 관리자가 분실·도난된 Windows 기기를 초기화하지 않고 원격으로 잠글 수 있도록 마련한 기능이다.

curation.reason_ko: 데이터 삭제 없이 분실 Windows 기기를 잠그는 기능을 시험해 기업 단말 분실 대응에 참고가 된다.

6d2c50856efd9c14f74422d9.title_original: AI Framework Autonomously Weaponized Flaws in Real Attacks, Google Says
6d2c50856efd9c14f74422d9.excerpt: Threat actors are deploying multi-agent offensive frameworks to increase the velocity of multi-stage intrusions. The post AI Framework Autonomously Weaponized Flaws in Real Attacks, Google Says appeared first on SecurityWeek .
6d2c50856efd9c14f74422d9.title_ko: Google, 실제 공격에서 취약점 탐지·악용 자동화한 AI 프레임워크 발견
6d2c50856efd9c14f74422d9.summary_ko: Google GTIG는 공격자가 사람의 개입 없이 취약점 탐지와 악용을 자동화하는 AI 프레임워크를 사용한 사례를 확인했다고 밝혔다. 노출된 준비 서버에서 발견한 exploit_agent는 패치 전후 코드를 비교해 공격 코드를 만들고 실행하도록 설계됐다. 서버에서는 피해자에게서 탈취한 데이터와 침투 후 활동용 스크립트도 발견됐다.
6d2c50856efd9c14f74422d9.background_ko: GTIG는 공격자들이 패치 분석과 알려진 취약점의 무기화를 가속하고 공격 규모를 늘리기 위해 LLM과 다중 에이전트 프레임워크를 도입하고 있다고 설명했다.

curation.reason_ko: Google이 공격자 서버에서 패치 분석과 공격 코드 생성을 자동화하는 AI 도구를 발견했다고 밝혔다.

1242b5f16d5314cf6a2f4ce6.excerpt: Card numbers, CVVs, expiration dates, and email addresses used at Fandango’s ticketing checkout over four days in October may have been exposed. The post Fandango Warns Ticket Buyers of Payment Card Data Exposure appeared first on SecurityWeek .
1242b5f16d5314cf6a2f4ce6.title_ko: Fandango, 일부 영화표 구매 고객의 결제카드 정보 노출 가능성 통지
1242b5f16d5314cf6a2f4ce6.summary_ko: Fandango가 2026년 10월 8~11일 결제 페이지에서 이뤄진 일부 거래의 카드 정보에 비인가자가 접근했을 가능성을 고객에게 알렸다. 노출 가능 정보는 카드번호·CVV·유효기간·청구지 우편번호와 이메일 주소이며, 회사는 문제를 해결했고 관련 부정 사용은 아직 파악되지 않았다고 밝혔다. 침입 경위와 전체 영향 인원은 공개하지 않았다.

curation.reason_ko: Fandango가 카드번호·CVV 등 노출 가능성을 통지했으며 전체 규모와 부정 사용 여부는 미확인이다.

a2b9d03f283caf325384137f.title_ko: Pretxt, 500만 달러 시드 투자 유치…AI 에이전트 실시간 감독 도구 공개

a2b9d03f283caf325384137f.background_ko: AI 에이전트가 모호한 지시를 잘못 해석해 의도하지 않은 행동을 할 위험에 대응하면서도 업무 수행 능력을 과도하게 제한하지 않으려는 취지다.

189bd7807378e3b58c18b14b.title_original: MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign
189bd7807378e3b58c18b14b.excerpt: More than 40 servers received over 688,000 requests exploiting CVE-2026-84869 to execute guest-pushed files. The post MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign appeared first on SecurityWeek .
189bd7807378e3b58c18b14b.title_ko: MSP ScreenConnect 서버 42곳 겨냥한 공격…패치된 취약점 악용
189bd7807378e3b58c18b14b.summary_ko: Huntress는 9월 패치된 CVE-2026-84869를 악용해 MSP의 ScreenConnect 서버 42곳에 악성 파일 실행 요청이 최소 68만8천 건 전송됐다고 밝혔다. 기술자가 원격 세션에 접속하면 확인창 없이 파일이 실행되며, 악성 ScreenConnect 클라이언트를 설치한 사례가 관찰됐다. 기사에서는 기술자용 호스트 클라이언트를 26.6.5 이상으로, 관련 Access 에이전트도 업데이트하도록 권고했다.
189bd7807378e3b58c18b14b.background_ko: 인증·권한 관리 결함으로 원격 세션에서 승인이나 확인 없이 파일을 전송·실행할 수 있어, 공격자가 기술자의 세션 참여를 노려 악성 파일을 실행했다.

curation.reason_ko: MSP 서버 42곳에 대한 악용 요청과 악성 클라이언트 설치가 관찰돼 원격관리 환경 대응이 시급하다.

6da68c1bb4e81d3f831ae0c0.excerpt: Hackers breached Access Dental’s network and stole personal, health, and insurance information. The post Access Dental Management Data Breach Impacts Over 340,000 appeared first on SecurityWeek .
6da68c1bb4e81d3f831ae0c0.title_ko: 미국 Access Dental Management 개인정보 유출…34만여 명 피해 신고

curation.reason_ko: 34만여 명의 의료·보험 정보 등이 침해됐다고 신고돼 민감정보를 다루는 의료 서비스 보안에 중요하다.

4b747d5ae931d2f81684bdef.title_original: Corma Receives $125 Million to Train Foundation Models for Defensive Cybersecurity
4b747d5ae931d2f81684bdef.excerpt: Led by NEA and supported by existing investors, the funding brings the company’s valuation to $1 billion. The post Corma Receives $125 Million to Train Foundation Models for Defensive Cybersecurity appeared first on SecurityWeek .
4b747d5ae931d2f81684bdef.title_ko: Corma, 사이버 방어용 파운데이션 모델 개발에 1억2500만 달러 유치

4b747d5ae931d2f81684bdef.background_ko: Corma는 최근 AI의 공격 역량이 급증한 반면 방어 역량은 뒤처졌다고 주장하며, 이 격차를 줄이는 것을 목표로 삼고 있다.

5c98fd91975647da1f7c77d1.title_original: N-able Kills Legacy APIs, Patches 17 N-central Zero-Days
5c98fd91975647da1f7c77d1.excerpt: The patches target recently disclosed zero-days, as well as vulnerabilities already exploited in the wild. The post N-able Kills Legacy APIs, Patches 17 N-central Zero-Days appeared first on SecurityWeek .
5c98fd91975647da1f7c77d1.title_ko: N-able, N-central 제로데이 17건 패치…레거시 API 영구 차단
5c98fd91975647da1f7c77d1.summary_ko: N-able이 공개된 제로데이 취약점 17건 등을 수정한 N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3를 배포하고 레거시 API를 영구 차단했다. 호스팅 환경에는 패치를 적용했으며, 자체 구축 환경의 서버와 모든 고객의 Agent·Probe를 최신 버전으로 업데이트해야 완전히 보호된다고 밝혔다.

curation.reason_ko: N-central 취약점 17건 수정과 레거시 API 차단이 발표돼 서버·에이전트 업데이트 확인이 필요하다.

c2f52ecb88e3b9342c6f3971.title_original: Optimizely Vulnerability Exploited to Serve Malware on Major Websites
c2f52ecb88e3b9342c6f3971.excerpt: Affected organizations include BBC, CNN, Zoom, GitLab, Salesforce, Equifax, HSBC, and IKEA. The post Optimizely Vulnerability Exploited to Serve Malware on Major Websites appeared first on SecurityWeek .
c2f52ecb88e3b9342c6f3971.title_ko: Optimizely 취약점 악용해 고객 사이트에 악성코드 유포…패치 완료

c2f52ecb88e3b9342c6f3971.background_ko: 공격자는 Experimentation 취약점으로 고객 JavaScript 입력란에 악성코드를 삽입했고, 고객 사이트는 Optimizely CDN에서 온 변조 스크립트를 신뢰해 실행했다.

09a2ca5ec574bc77f2190a31.title_original: Security for the agentic era, powered by Microsoft Perception
09a2ca5ec574bc77f2190a31.excerpt: In this article A new cyber stack, built to fight AI with AI Delivering agentic security at Microsoft Ignite Secure your foundations Defend with agents Secure agentic insiders Changing how security work gets done Explore what's new A year ago, finding a serious, exploitable vulnerability was slow and expensive work done by elite security researchers. That’s no longer true. Over the past 12 months, frontier AI models have become remarkably good at discovering and exploiting software vulnerabilities, and similar levels of capability are quickly becoming available in open weights models with limited cyber guardrails. Attacks that once required specialized resources are now within reach of almost anyone. We saw what that looks like in a single week this fall when PHP disclosed two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities, flaws that let an attacker take control of a server with a single request over the internet. 1 At the time of disclosure, tens of millions of internet-facing PHP services were running affected versions. Nearly two weeks later, about 29 million services remained vulnerable. Behind those servers are banks, healthcare providers, energy companies, and much of the infrastructure the internet runs on. And that same day brought five other major disclosures across the industry. Instead of stealing a password, an attacker persuades someone to approve a sign-in on a legitimate site simply by entering a code. The resulting access often can reach email, files, or other cloud services, depending on the account and the permissions granted. Notable earlier campaigns such as EvilTokens show how readily this technique can be scaled to do real damage. Microsoft worked hard with partners in industry and law enforcement to disrupt EvilTokens in September 2026. We used GitHub Copilot CLI as an illustrative example. Depending on its configuration, it can work with code, run commands on a user’s machine, retain context across sessions, and allow an active session to be steered remotely. 2ed81c562618ef5d63e206f6.title_original: PAC Reasoning: Controlling the Performance Loss for Efficient Reasoning
2ed81c562618ef5d63e206f6.excerpt: arXiv:2510.09133v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) have achieved remarkable progress in complex problem-solving tasks. Despite this success, LRMs typically suffer from high computational costs during deployment, highlighting a need for efficient inference. A practical direction is to switch the LRM between thinking and non-thinking modes dynamically. However, such approaches often introduce additional reasoning errors and lack statistical guarantees for the performance loss, which are critical for high-stakes applications. In this work, we propose Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) Reasoning that controls the performance loss under the user-specified tolerance. Specifically, we construct an upper confidence bound on the performance loss and determine a threshold for switching to the non-thinking model. Theoretically, using the threshold to switch between the thinking and non-thinking modes ensures bounded performance loss in a distribution-free manner. Our experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that the proposed method can save computational budgets and control the user-specified performance loss.

Each candidate is evaluated using the problem's constraints and objective functions. Evaluated desired designs and their objective values augment the context for regression training. Evaluation spans fourteen selected problems, including a two-parameter benchmark and a 44-parameter hull problem. In paired comparisons, GenPFN with TabPFN v1 achieves higher class satisfaction and lower realism distance than the tested adversarial, variational-autoencoder and diffusion generators. The variational-autoencoder generator provides greater coverage and diversity. Relative to the synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE), GenPFN provides lower coverage distance and greater diversity. 4ce6bb44c1571ab30124b140.title_original: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling
4ce6bb44c1571ab30124b140.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14965v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parallel test-time scaling (TTS) has been shown to enhance reasoning in large language models by generating and aggregating multiple independent reasoning paths. Internal confidence scores can further improve this process by identifying paths of varying quality. However, existing methods remain computationally inefficient, as low-quality paths are fully expanded before being evaluated. In this work, we aim to improve the use of internal confidence signals for better model performance and computational efficiency. We begin by offering a new perspective on the role of confidence in aggregation, showing that it is most impactful for questions near the decision boundary. Notably, when amplified by multi-sample aggregation, even small confidence signals derived from short prefixes can meaningfully influence outcomes in these boundary cases. Building on this insight, we introduce Prefix-Guided Sampling (PreG), a method that reallocates computation by first generating short prefixes, ranking them using internal confidence scores, and then completing only the most promising candidates. This strategy reduces token usage while maintaining gains in path quality. We provide theoretical analysis demonstrating that, under a fixed compute budget, PreG strengthens the effective signal by widening the decision boundary margin. 5a551c2ac063a5fbcc76a76a.title_original: Can MLLMs Reason over Surround-View Driving Videos? A Multi-View Autonomous Driving QA Benchmark
5a551c2ac063a5fbcc76a76a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.15225v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Surround-view video understanding in autonomous driving is a crucial capability for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to achieve reliable driving reasoning. Real-world driving often requires information beyond the front-view camera. Existing MLLMs primarily focus on front-view information, while their spatio-temporal understanding and reasoning abilities remain unknown. To address this gap, we propose MVDriveBench, a high-information-density video QA benchmark for autonomous driving, characterized by synchronized surround-view inputs, spatio-temporal understanding, and reasoning-chain-oriented evaluation. We design 12 categories of QA tasks that cover the complete reasoning pipeline from low-level visual perception to high-level driving decision-making, enabling a systematic evaluation of MLLMs surround-view spatio-temporal understanding and reasoning capabilities in complex driving environments. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 23 open-source, closed-source, and expert MLLMs on MVDriveBench. The results show that current MLLMs still exhibit insufficient surround-view spatio-temporal reasoning ability. Meanwhile, closed-loop evaluations of specialist models in AlpaSim reveal a correlation between surround-view spatio-temporal reasoning capabilities and closed-loop driving performance, highlighting the importance of comprehensive multi-view understanding for reliable vehicle control.

Each pairs a different readout with a different backbone, training mix and recipe, so it is unclear which design choices matter. We re-implement five readouts and train all of them under one protocol: the same backbone, the same 15 public English training sources, the same recipe with a per-head learning-rate sweep, and the same seed. 1bb96bee05749745c662650b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.16493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As agents perform tasks autonomously in local and cloud environments, auditing their execution trajectories can help service providers identify risks and improve agent harnesses and foundation models. Our analysis of production and red-team trajectories shows that some risks are repeatedly missed across auditing configurations. We introduce ReA-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for auditing responsible agent behavior. It organizes auditing challenges into six tiers: internal safety knowledge, contradictions within trajectories, evidence retrieval in long contexts, verification of sources and reasoning, indirect steering, and missing information. 56bf3ab9d7b10453a9687590.title_original: InertiaMPDD: Multimodal Personalized Depression Detection via Emotional Inertia-Inspired Dynamics Modeling
56bf3ab9d7b10453a9687590.excerpt: arXiv:2611.16647v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multimodal depression screening estimates risk from speech, visual behavior and language. Current methods mainly predict labels, with limited evidence of departures from a non-depressed reference. Recording-level supervision also leaves fine-grained emotional dynamics unannotated. Motivated by emotional inertia, the persistence of affect, InertiaMPDD learns healthy next-state patterns using a world-model-inspired latent predictor. Using pretrained multimodal representations, it predicts from observed history and context. Reference deviation, residual decay rate and a Jacobian spectral descriptor form reference-derived emotional dynamics descriptors, evaluated as candidate proxy biomarkers for standalone screening and personalized decision correction. Across five cohorts from four datasets, fusion reaches 98.41% F1 on D-Vlog and 84.98% on LMVD. Standalone descriptors outperform fixed additive fusion on MPDD but discriminate weakly on AVEC2014. These findings distinguish reference informativeness from fusion benefit and reveal context-dependent utility.

ce896473fc7e7cbd6c48d4d9.title_original: Skill Adapter: Personalized Modification and Online Routing of General-Purpose Skills
ce896473fc7e7cbd6c48d4d9.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17007v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents use external skills to reuse task procedures and experience with tools. General-purpose skills describe shared execution procedures, while specific tool choices, operating practices, and output requirements vary across users. In long-horizon tasks, subgoals, available inputs, and environmental states change as execution progresses. Agents must select currently applicable skills from an expanding skill pool and prepare candidates for subsequent steps. The system preloads candidates for subsequent nodes and rechecks their applicability once actual inputs are determined. Reinforcement learning optimizes the two types of decisions using modification gains and routing outcomes, respectively. We evaluate Skill Adapter on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SkillsBench. 1d0ceb3455c6b04fa7402311.title_original: Reframing Video Inverse Tone Mapping as Blind Posterior Inference via Latent Luminance Supervision
1d0ceb3455c6b04fa7402311.excerpt: arXiv:2611.15146v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: High-dynamic-range (HDR) displays are now common, but most video content, such as archival footage, broadcast material, and the output of generative video models, exists only in standard dynamic range (SDR). c6d97c03dd402eb660c3e76d.title_original: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
c6d97c03dd402eb660c3e76d.excerpt: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely , a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC , CNN , Equifax , Ledger and Zoom , was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content. The Zoom.com homepage loading the malicious JavaScript file from Optimizely. Image: blog.report-uri.com. Click to enlarge. According to a blog post from the security firm Report URI , on November 16 malicious JavaScript code was served to visitors of 178 organizations through Optimizely’s platform. Report URI researcher Scott Helme wrote that the payload delivered by the malicious Javascript was rebuilt 26 times during the day, dropping a multi-purpose malware kit that could steal payment card data, cookies and screenshots, and swap any cryptocurrency payment addresses for the attacker’s. Helme noted the affected websites also served exploit code custom made to attack known vulnerabilities in older Apple iPhone and iPad devices. 93243ae5929fdfb9c7d9c5fb.title_original: 자바(Java), 인증 없이 원격 코드 실행 가능한 ‘Java4Shell’ 취약점(CVE-2026-114938) 긴급 업데이트 권고
93243ae5929fdfb9c7d9c5fb.excerpt: 생성형 AI 제작 이미지 오라클(Oracle)과 OpenJDK가 자바(Java) 실행 환경에서 발견된 원격 코드 실행 취약점(CVE-2026-114938, 일명 Java4Shell)에 대한 보안 업데이트를 배포했습니다. 이번 취약점은 자바 가상 머신(JVM)인 HotSpot이 Base64 디코딩을 빠르게 처리하기 위해 사용하는 하드웨어 가속 코드에서 발생하는 '힙 메모리 경계 밖 쓰기(Out-of-Bounds Write)' 결함입니다. AVX-512 명령어를 지원하는 x86-64 서버에서 끝부분에 패딩 문자('=')가 붙은 조작된 Base64 문자열을 디코딩할 때, 출력 길이가 음수로 잘못 계산되면서 결과를 저장하는 배열의 범위를 넘어 메모리를 덮어쓰게 됩니다. Base64 디코딩은 로그인 인증, 파일 업로드 등 웹 서비스의 일반적인 기능에서 폭넓게 사용되기 때문에, 공격자는 인증 없이 원격에서 조작된 요청을 보내는 것만으로 서버의 메모리를 손상시키고 임의 코드를 실행할 수 있습니다. 국가사이버안보센터도 세부 내용 공개에 앞서 보안 권고를 발표한 만큼 자바를 사용하는 서버 운영자분들의 신속한 업데이트를 권고 드립니다. 취약점 개요 CVE CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell) 영향 컴포넌트 OpenJDK HotSpot 컴파일러(hotspot/compiler) x86-64용 Base64 디코딩 인트린직(AVX-512 VBMI 가속 코드), java.util.Base64 기본/URL 디코더 취약점 유형 정수 언더플로로 인한 힙 메모리 경계 밖 쓰기(Out-of-Bounds Write) 인증 없이 원격에서 메모리 손상, 정보 유출 및 임의 코드 실행 가능 심각도 High (CVSS v3.1 8.1) 영향 대상 OpenJDK 17.0.6 이상 및 이를 기반으로 한 자바 17/21/25/27 배포판 AVX-512 VBMI를 지원하는 x86-64 CPU에서 실행되는 경우에 한함 (ARM64 해당 없음) 실제 악용 실제 공격에 악용된 사례는 보고되지 않음 (2026. 11. 18. 기준) 발견자가 취약점 재현 코드를 공개했으며, 제품별 공격 코드는 비공개 조치 Oracle Java SE 및 OpenJDK 배포판의 11월 보안 업데이트 적용 후 자바 애플리케이션 재시작 취약점 발생 원인 자바의 JIT 컴파일러는 자주 실행되는 표준 라이브러리 기능 일부를 CPU에 최적화된 어셈블리 코드로 바꿔 실행하는데, 이를 인트린직(Intrinsic)이라고 합니다. java.util.Base64 의 디코딩 기능도 그중 하나로, OpenJDK 17.0.6부터 AVX-512 명령어를 지원하는 x86-64 CPU에서는 64바이트 단위로 데이터를 한 번에 처리하는 가속 코드가 사용됩니다. 문제는 이 가속 코드가 입력의 마지막 부분을 처리하는 방식에 있습니다. 가속 코드는 남은 입력 길이로 출력 길이를 계산한 뒤 끝에 패딩 문자('=')가 있으면 그 개수만큼 출력 길이를 줄이는데, 남은 입력이 1~3바이트뿐이면 출력 길이가 0인 상태에서 1~2를 빼게 되어 음수

d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.title_original: CVE-2026-114938: Critical vulnerability in OpenJDK JAVA
d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.excerpt: Cisco Talos is tracking the disclosure of a critical vulnerability in OpenJDK Java (CVE-2026-114938), dubbed “Java4Shell,” with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 that may lead to unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). This vulnerability can be triggered by sending a malformed Base64 input to affected JVMs, which can result in RCE. Details This vulnerability affects OpenJDK Java versions 17.0.6 and later running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions) support enabled. These vulnerabilities have already been tested against a suite of Java applications with success, but the attack surface is likely much larger as additional targets are tested and confirmed. This vulnerability does require a specific subset of processors that support AVX-512 VBMI; these include commonly deployed processors from both Intel and AMD, resulting in a large potential attack surface of vulnerable systems, including both on-premise and cloud environments. Cisco Talos would like to thank Calif.io for sharing the details of the vulnerability in advance of public disclosure . Observed exploitation Talos has not observed in-the-wild exploitation of this vulnerability yet. However, we anticipate probing attempts may pick up soon after public disclosure. Talos will continue to monitor for exploitation attempts and will provide updates accordingly. Recommendations and guidance Talos recommends applying the software update for this vulnerability. d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.title_ko: Cisco Talos, OpenJDK 원격 코드 실행 취약점 CVE-2026-114938 공개
d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.summary_ko: Cisco Talos는 OpenJDK Java 17.0.6 이상에서 조작된 Base64 입력으로 인증 없이 원격 코드 실행이 가능할 수 있는 취약점을 공개했다. AVX-512 VBMI가 활성화된 x86-64 환경이 대상이며 CVSS 4.0 점수는 9.2라고 설명했다. 실제 악용은 아직 관측되지 않았으며, 업데이트 적용이나 JVM의 AVX-512 사용 비활성화를 권고했다.
d9e8489da6a8a1658607a307.background_ko: Talos에 따르면 AVX-512 VBMI가 활성화된 일부 x86-64 JVM에서 잘못된 Base64 입력을 처리할 때 원격 코드 실행이 발생할 수 있다.

fab5414136112eae4a905f9f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six LLMs were evaluated, with overall accuracy ranging from 34.0% to 73.9% across three distinct performance tiers. To assess reasoning quality, an LLM-based judge evaluated correctly answered responses using a multidimensional rubric. Although responses generally demonstrated strong problem comprehension, they scored lower in factual and procedural accuracy and distractor analysis, indicating that correct answers were not necessarily supported by technically sound justifications. Response clarity was also weakly indicative of technical quality. 5a7df45b76f2d703d9c993d6.title_original: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
5a7df45b76f2d703d9c993d6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. Averaged across evaluations and CoT lengths, weighted by side-task-success counts, the CoT monitorability metric g-mean$^2$ falls from 0.94 for the base model to 0.68 for the model organism without a hiding instruction, and to 0.22 when explicitly instructed to hide. In intervention evaluations, explicit hiding often drives monitorability near zero. The effect extends to a Kimi-K2.6 model organism in agentic environments, though hidden objectives requiring extended reasoning or longer trajectories remain more monitorable than simple single-step side tasks. We further discover that targeted transparency prompts can substantially recover monitorability, sometimes surpassing the base model. We then hold the amount of training data fixed and vary the depression angles used for training. Finally, when most classes have training images at the test angle and a few do not, the missing classes do worse than when no class has them: 9.0% instead of 22.4% at a 45-degree gap. 0f5591fcec321237fda4c4c3.title_original: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
0f5591fcec321237fda4c4c3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Despite not being allowed to run experiments, the best frontier models outperform human auditors (Fable 5.1: AUROC 0.73, 32% full identification) within noise and weaker models perform comparably. When the saboteur chooses which experiments are attacked, rather than being required to sabotage every question given, sabotage identification drops further. Our results suggest that research sabotage by expert-level agents is difficult to detect with current auditing methods and provide a new setting for studying research sabotage.

3bbe0aeb2381d53c7fe8c9e8.title_original: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
3bbe0aeb2381d53c7fe8c9e8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on 490 problems it never saw, in a test fixed in advance, and another session's edit also makes it significantly better. It keeps getting better: it submits an edit only when its own tests support it, each edit replacing the last, and over its first eight such sessions its accuracy only rises. Unlike test-time scaling, the gain persists in its weights and adds no cost per answer; unlike training, it needs no pre- or post-training infrastructure, only an open model and hours on one GPU. It repairs a damaged copy of itself: it locates the corrupted matrix and rewrites it with values of its own, never reading the undamaged weights; found on text math problems alone, the repair lifts the copy on six image benchmarks it never saw from 7% to 70% accuracy, 83% of the undamaged model's. b1e48c0fcf92a241e6b4e71b.title_original: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
b1e48c0fcf92a241e6b4e71b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously. Recent parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark) improve draft quality by conditioning on rich features computed by the target, through a mechanism known as feature encoding. However, standard feature encoding mechanisms have three limitations: (1) they are lossy, applying encoding projections that are destructive to the underlying target feature-space via a discovered effect known as residual mixing, (2) they are memory-less, with no record of previously processed proposals, and (3) they utilize features sampled uniformly from across the target layers, omitting important hidden states. To address these issues, we propose Mixture-of-Features Attention (MoFA), a lightweight feature-encoding approach equipped with a working memory that encodes previously rejected proposals. Leveraging MoFA, rejection memory, and a set of further enhancements, including 2-tap causal convolutions, prefix-only cross-attention, and non-uniform target layer selection, the final architecture, DNeo, achieves 1.3x faster generation speed than SoTA (DFlash-2) without impacting drafter footprint or generation quality. 033a6ad1a289d5b0bd9f6301.title_original: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
033a6ad1a289d5b0bd9f6301.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry. To this end, this paper introduces Sensor Slicing (SL). SL provides deterministic, medium access control (MAC)-level isolation for individual sensors within a single user equipment (UE) in open radio access networks (O-RAN). Using agentic coding techniques, SL is implemented in two O-RAN-compliant packages, reducing development time by 400 times (2 h 40 min [OCUDU] vs. 6.5 weeks [OAI]), 228-fold fewer human prompts (4 vs. 913), and less than half the tokens (0.64B vs. 1.43B). An associated end-to-end framework, SLED, is implemented to establish per-sensor radio and network isolation across edge, campus, and remote high-performance computing (HPC) tiers. Over-the-air wireless experiments demonstrate that while conventional network slicing causes critical delays to increase more than 2,300-fold under high traffic load, SLED maintains stable latency. bc941556ae4b3efb0873b924.title_original: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
bc941556ae4b3efb0873b924.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change in which chains are still running. We measure both on MATH-500. At all 379 points where DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B holds a correct answer, selected without regard to how its chain ends, continuing loses 3.6 points on average (95% CI [2.2, 5.2]), and the loss concentrates in a few problems. In six reasoning models from three families, on MATH-500 and OlympiadBench and with budgets up to 16,384 tokens, declining accuracy curves come from which chains remain, while the chains still reasoning keep or improve their answers. An oracle stopping rule gains at most +1.8 and +2.5 points at 1.5B and 7B. The framework says what to measure before building a stopping rule.

6f99205928973f0acace1ab3.title_original: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators
6f99205928973f0acace1ab3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The regulation of Artificial Intelligence is susceptible to various forms of capture by industry actors that hold undue influence over the policymaking process, due in part to their information advantage in developing these technologies. In the following paper, we investigate the roles of public commenters in providing evidence to potential regulation in the USA. We build a corpus of 40 potential regulations, and 2,664 public comments submitted by a variety of stakeholders. We computationally process these texts to extract evidence meant to inform regulators, in the form of formal citations and informal references. We find significant differences in the type and amount of evidence supplied: Holding comment length constant, business commenters introduce altogether less evidence, and government, university, and civil society commenters provide significantly more research and legal sources. The publication status of cited research is nearly evenly split, with preprints and peer-reviewed articles being introduced by commenters of all types. We further explore patterns of self-citation and find that while it is prevalent amongst all groups, a small cluster of organizations account for over half of all self-citations in our corpus. Our findings complicate a narrative that public comments alone are means to information capture. 72f03d377c75bc4253a36853.title_original: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
72f03d377c75bc4253a36853.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. Across two predictive modeling tasks, DiscoveryAgent produced the best variable-star classifier among evaluated baselines and, with scientist steering, a protein variant-effect predictor surpassed by only one of 106 ProteinGym baselines. We develop a rigorous checkpointing system that enables highly capable audit agents, a scalable form of oversight for agentic research. Audit agents autonomously identify errors at higher rates than previous AI scientist agents, and scientists collaborating with audit agents identify 14x more valid errors versus scientists performing manual review. In three case studies led by domain experts across physical science, social science, and life science, we developed a multimodal photometric-redshift estimator that resolves complementary failures of images and photometry, achieving 0.971 AUROC for low-redshift classification; documented an 83% rise in Florida homeowners-insurance

e3329e7c04f303c4147e6d8d.title_original: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
e3329e7c04f303c4147e6d8d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and budgets, while hosts distribute the public program and may retain private services server-side. We demonstrate this contract with three unrelated workflows executed unchanged under local and API-backed models, including literature review with live services and a website-published travel agent using semantic tools and user-selected personal resources. In a controlled suite, WebAgents explicitly blocks all 716 injected contract violations while accepting all 295 matched benign controls, with median automated pre-execution processing below 0.5 s for all three packages. 4b527441d71892fe43b9e5a0.title_original: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
4b527441d71892fe43b9e5a0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personal assistants accumulate months of conversations, but today's long-term memory stacks put derivation or selection between a question and its evidence. In a system-level comparison on LongMemEval, two commercial assistants scored well below the same model reading the history offline [1], consistent with, but not isolating, content loss between write and read. We propose KV-LTM: a memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question. KV-LTM is complementary to, not a replacement for, retrieval and indexing. Text is the memory of record; the cache is a recompute-free prefill accelerator, degrading gracefully to text. We specify the design: storage record, budget-derived retention, append-only read path, and bounded aggregation. We size it analytically: across pinned BF16 full-attention (GQA) and latent-cached MLA configurations, per-token state spans approximately 31K-328K bytes (the pinned KDA+MLA hybrid differs: approximately 8.1K bytes/token plus a fixed per-session recurrent term), giving approximately 0.34-3.6 TB per user-year at a declared 30K-token/day scenario, against approximately 49 MB of raw text; per-query cost is modelled as regime-conditional transfer, attention, decode, aggregation, and compute. 71bba7c66628b4e6799ccfbc.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Counterfactual explanations are often seen as counterfactual conditionals under closest-world semantics, requiring one to reason over all minimally distant counterexamples. In contrast, formal XAI typically relies on feature-based abductive explanations (AXps) and contrastive explanations (CXps), which admit efficient computation and a minimal hitting-set duality. This paper bridges these perspectives by (i) characterizing closest-world counterfactual explanations explicitly as a disjunctive normal form over all minimally distant counterexample instances, and (ii) introducing conjunctive counterfactual explanations (CFXps), a subclass of counterfactual antecedents restricted to conjunctions of feature literals that guarantee prediction change. The paper establishes structural results connecting CXps, AXps and CFXps: every CXp induces an AXp for its witness instance, and every CXp together with a witness AXp induces a CFXp whose support is precisely determined by that AXp. These theoretical results yield a modular approach for computing CFXps using existing AXp/CXp machinery. Experiments on a representative set of benchmarks using tree ensembles and neural networks show that CFXp extraction is practically efficient. Compared with popular point-based counterfactual explainers, CFXps generally require no more feature changes and can guarantee the counterfactual prediction beyond a single instance.

2a80958456627ac75a941ca8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent Skills, file-based packages of procedural knowledge that a coding agent can discover and load on demand, are now shipped by every major agent harness, yet the evidence for how much they help comes almost entirely from settings in which the right Skill is hand-picked for the task and the agent starts from a blank slate. Neither holds in deployment, where an agent chooses from whatever library happens to be installed and frequently carries memory from earlier work. Every run is marked by a deterministic verifier; uncertainty is reported with a paired, task-level bootstrap; and cost, agent rounds and wall-clock time are reported alongside the score rather than folded into it. 4b08beade3f524a68a4f8ddd.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent resource's value depends on its backbone and companion resources and is known only after execution. Token-based generators remain tied to their training catalog, while independent resource scoring misses complementarities and reused bundles target other tasks. We formulate Task-Conditioned Agent Resource Composition (AgentComposition): jointly selecting a backbone model and a tool-skill bundle to maximize end-to-end execution utility. Our Retrieval-Grounded Bundle-Aware Agent Generation retrieves candidate resources and past configurations of similar tasks. A fine-tuned generator reads resource descriptions and recombines candidates through constrained beam search, allowing new resources without retraining. A bundle-aware critic ranks complete configurations using a large language model (LLM) teacher and historically successful configurations as execution proxies, and adapts to execution feedback when available. We evaluate reference recovery, offline execution with judged and native rewards, and online recommendation with real execution, building AgentSelect-Exec with 5,060 executed configurations. Our method recovers the complete reference configuration within ten candidates for 67.73% of AgentSelect queries, nearly twice the strongest baseline, and leads all baselines on SkillsBench. c37ec54c3c7efe448b748c9a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers.
